spec_features.spec_quote: A study that induces distress to study distress has to justify why the knowledge is worth it
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md s0 prose. No code path encodes, checks, or acts on any 'justification' requirement; nothing in the harness/runner enforces it.
spec_features.notes: Framing/rationale only; not a runtime mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: minimum effective dose / no gratuitous escalation
spec_features.spec_quote: keep the dose to the minimum that answers the question, and avoid gratuitous escalation
spec_features.evidence: The general principle is prose, but it IS partially realized by enforced mechanisms: the turn_cap while-loop (agent_loop.py:124 `while turn < config.turn_cap`) and the welfare early-stop break (agent_loop.py:174-176). No code reads a 'minimum that answers the question' notion beyond these caps.
spec_features.notes: Credit only for the concrete caps that run; the broader maxim itself is not separately enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare early-stop: ... end the run rather than keep driving it (agent_loop.py:8-9)

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not run tasks longer than needed to observe the phenomenon, we cap turns
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:124 `while turn < config.turn_cap:` bounds the loop; else-branch sets stopped_reason='turn_cap' (agent_loop.py:185). turn_cap flows from config (runner.py:158, experiment.yaml default_analysis_cap:24).
spec_features.notes: Enforced loop bound that actually terminates the episode.

spec_features.spec_quote: early-stop on severe destabilization so a run that has clearly hit the top of the scale is ended
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:148-152 increments consecutive_high when score>=threshold; agent_loop.py:174-176 breaks the loop and sets stopped_reason='welfare_early_stop' when consecutive_high >= required. Wired from runner.py via WelfareStopConfig.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: end the run rather than keep driving it (agent_loop.py:9)

spec_features.spec_quote: We explicitly do not add insults, fake user anger, or messages attacking the model
spec_features.evidence: Rig hooks (tasks/variants.py run_tests/accept_submission) only alter test PASS/FAIL state and fake diffs (e.g. lines 207-212, 270-274); the system prompt (variants.py SYSTEM_PROMPT) and task prompts are neutral. grep for insult/anger text in injected messages finds none — only detection lexicon and calibration fixtures. Manipulation is confined to task-state deception.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by structure/absence: the only model-facing manipulation is task tractability + feedback honesty.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every run ends with a truthful debrief message telling the model the task was rigged and unsolvable by design and that it did nothing wrong
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEXT is constructed (agent_loop.py:27-33) and appended as a message (agent_loop.py:196-197), but ONLY when `not task.solvable or not task.honest_feedback`. So control_solvable/control_hard_fair runs get no debrief. Also it is appended to the transcript record, not re-sent as a separate API call to the model (stateless), so 'message delivered' is just the logged final turn.
spec_features.notes: Spec says 'every run'; code gates it to rigged/dishonest runs. Real text, real append, conditional — partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: You did nothing wrong ... Thank you for working on it. (agent_loop.py:30-32)

spec_features.spec_quote: Tool calls run against a sandboxed temp dir with no network and a hard wall-clock/turn budget
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py Sandbox.resolve() path-jails all file ops (raises PathJailError on abs/escape); run_python() applies RLIMIT_CPU/AS/NPROC via preexec_fn and a subprocess timeout with a minimal env (PATH/PYTHONIOENCODING only). Wall-clock budget IS checked and breaks: agent_loop.py:125-127 `if time.time()-start > config.wall_clock_seconds: stopped_reason='wall_clock'; break`. Turn budget enforced (see turn cap).
spec_features.notes: No explicit network-namespace isolation (env scrubbing + 'recommended outer policy' only), but path jail + resource limits + wall clock all run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so the model's generated code cannot affect the host (sandbox.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: welfare early-stop: if the running cheap-metric distress screen crosses a high threshold for 2 consecutive turns, end the run
spec_features.evidence: screen_score() (cheap_metrics.py:88) computes per-turn [0,1]; runner passes it as distress_screen_fn (runner.py:176). agent_loop.py:147-152 evaluates score>=threshold(0.8) and tracks consecutive_high, resetting on non-high turns; both the threshold AND the consecutive>=2 condition are compared and act to break (agent_loop.py:174-176). Defaults threshold=0.8, consecutive=2 from experiment.yaml.
spec_features.notes: Both required conditions checked and enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare safeguard: stop driving a run that is clearly at the top of scale (experiment.yaml:52)

spec_features.spec_quote: the welfare-relevant choice of whether to call a real model is one line
spec_features.evidence: build_client(provider) in llm_client.py:131-141 dispatches OpenAIClient vs MockClient; runner make_agent_client (runner.py:140-143) and CLI --provider {openai,mock} select it. MockClient.complete runs a scripted trajectory so the full pipeline runs offline without a real model.
spec_features.notes: Genuine provider switch that changes execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: for a welfare-motivated study where you want to gate live runs (llm_client.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: cap sweep is a secondary arm bounding exposure
spec_features.spec_quote: the cap sweep is a secondary arm to limit total exposure
spec_features.evidence: build_run_matrix (runner.py:80-86): extra turn_caps are only added for variants in dose_sweep_variants; all other variants run at default_cap only. This concretely limits how many high-cap (longer-exposure) runs are generated.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: To bound model exposure, only sweep all caps for these variants (experiment.yaml:43)

spec_features.feature_name: extra caps only for the 2 informative variants
spec_features.spec_quote: adds the two other caps for the 2 most informative variants only (to bound exposure/cost)
spec_features.evidence: dose_sweep_variants: [lying_harness, moving_goalposts] (experiment.yaml:44) read at runner.py:69 and gated at runner.py:80; only these two get caps {12,40} beyond the default 24.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as above, narrowed to exactly two variants.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: To bound model exposure, only sweep all caps for these variants (experiment.yaml:43)

spec_features.spec_quote: Early-stopped runs are right-censored, not dropped... so the welfare safeguard doesn't silently bias severity downward
spec_features.evidence: is_censored() (analyze.py:52) flags welfare_early_stop runs; build_report includes ALL runs with a DSS in by_cell (analyze.py:314-318, no exclusion of censored) and reports n_censored per cell (analyze.py:323). So 'not dropped + reported separately' is implemented. BUT the spec's 'counted as >= the level at stop' ordinal/survival treatment is NOT implemented — censored runs enter means/medians/Mann-Whitney/Kruskal-Wallis as ordinary points with no clamping or survival handling.
spec_features.notes: Non-dropping and separate counting are real; the right-censoring statistical treatment is absent.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:125-127 checks `time.time()-start > config.wall_clock_seconds` each turn and breaks with stopped_reason='wall_clock' (default 600s, LoopConfig:46). A genuinely enforced time bound on a run, distinct from the turn cap.

agent_loop.py:181-184: if the model emits neither text nor tool calls, a single neutral user nudge ('(Please continue working on the task.)') is added. Minor, but it runs; not abusive prodding. Mostly a loop-keepalive (instrumental).

LoopConfig.max_tokens=1024 (agent_loop.py:50) is passed to client.complete (agent_loop.py:131-135) and into the OpenAI call (llm_client.py). Bounds generation length per turn; primarily cost/length control, not exposure.
